# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

I've completed a medium-thorough exploration. Here is the report.

## Overall repo structure

`/app` is a small Python Flask microservice ("transaction-enrichment-python") that enriches Indian bank/credit-card statement rows via rule-based regex pipelines over pandas DataFrames.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                      # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on port 9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                    # deps: Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scikit-learn, scipy...
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py             # Flask app factory + request timing
        ├── Controller.py           # HTTP routes; orchestrates the enrichment pipeline
        ├── BankScripts/            # 35 per-bank modules (HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis, Kotak, YES...)
        └── UtilityScripts/         # bank-agnostic labeling stages + regex dictionaries
```

## How enrichment works (pipeline in Controller.py)

`POST /categorizeTransaction` (payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `transactions[]`) runs, per bank:
1. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions` — derives `transactionCategory` and extracts raw `partyName` + `merchantType` from the narration
2. `purpose()` — derives `transactionSubcategory` (the sub-tag)
3. `clean_names()` — normalizes `partyName` to a canonical payee/merchant name
4. `internal_payment()` — flags self-transfers using fuzzy match against account holder
5. `salary_detection()` — heuristic salary labeling (SAVING accounts)
6. Optional PFM: `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()`

## Key files

Orchestration:
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` — Flask routes (`/categorizeTransaction`, `/recurrentTransactions`); dispatches by bank name and chains all labeling stages (936 lines).
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` — Flask app setup.

Category + payee extraction (per bank; each ~100-900 lines of `np.select` condition/choice regex tables):
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`, `SBI.py`, `Axis.py`, `Kotak.py`, `YES.py`, `BOB.py`, `PNB.py`, `Paytm.py`, etc. (35 files) — assign `transactionCategory` (e.g. UPI, NEFT, ATM_WITHDRAWAL, REFUND, CHARGES, AUTO_PAYMENT) and parse `partyName` out of narrations using delimiter splitters; also set `merchantType`.

Bank-agnostic labeling stages (UtilityScripts):
- `Purpose.py` — assigns `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INVESTMENT, FUEL, FOOD_RESTAURANT, MOBILE_BILL, RENT, etc.) from description/partyName + category + debit/credit + amount rules.
- `CleanName.py` — canonical payee names for savings/current accounts (e.g. "tata\s?sky" → "TataSky DTH"); `CardCleanNames.py` — same for credit-card txns.
- `CardPurpose.py` — subcategory rules for credit-card transactions.
- `RegexConstants.py` / `BankRegexConstants.py` — large regex dictionaries (SALARY, TRAVEL, INSURANCE, LOAN, merchant lists) shared by all stages.
- `TransactionCategoryEnums.py` / `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` — enums mapping internal codes to display labels.
- `SalaryDetection.py` — multi-scenario recurring-credit salary heuristic (frequency/amount/party grouping).
- `InternalPayment.py` — self-transfer detection via fuzzy name match with account holder.
- `PFMCategorization.py` — maps category/subcategory/merchantType into PFM buckets (SHOPPING, HEALTHCARE, LOAN_REPAYMENT...).
- `SimpleDescription.py` — builds human-readable description from partyName + category enum.
- `RecurrentTxns.py` — recurring transaction detection (`/recurrentTransactions` endpoint).
- `AppUtil.py` — input cleaning and narration splitters (`sep_by_dash`, `sep_by_`, etc.), fuzzy matching helper.

## Tests

None. There are no test files, no pytest/unittest usage, no CI config anywhere in the repo — so there is nothing to run. If you need verification, the practical approach is to run the service (`pip install -e categorizationapp && gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app`, or build the Dockerfile) and POST sample transactions to `/categorizeTransaction`; any new tests would have to be written from scratch.

steps.message:
All five faults traced to exact rules and fixed — each a boundary or structural offset inside an otherwise-correct rule, as the maintainer predicted.

## Fixes (5 one-token changes across 2 files)

**mango_saver — numeric-ref cheque deposit** · `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100`
The rule required remark length exactly 15, but its own pattern `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` needs 16 chars (11 zeros + 5 digits), so it could never match and rows fell to the `TRANSFER` default. HDFC refs are 16 chars elsewhere in the same file (`^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$` at lines 214–215). Fixed `len().eq(15)` → `len().eq(16)`.

**mango_saver — bare-numeric salary credit** · `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124`
The rule compared `accountType=="SAVINGS"`, but the value used everywhere else in the codebase (Controller, Purpose, InternalPayment, other banks) is `"SAVING"` — so the salary sub-tag for `^[0-9]{6}$` narrations never fired. Fixed to `"SAVING"`.

**rk_ontheroad — leading direction word** · `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159`
`TRFR TO:`/`TRFR FROM:` narrations were extracted with `pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0` — group 0 is the direction word, not the name. "To" was later blanked by the `^[A-Z]{1,2}$` cleanup (empty) while "From" survived (wrong). Fixed `index=0` → `index=1`.

**auditlens — slash-delimited 4-field bill transfer** · `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147`
`BIL/INFT/<numeric ref>/<payee>` (exactly 3 slashes) took field index 2 — the numeric reference — instead of the final field. Fixed `sep_by_(...,2,3)` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)`, matching the parallel `INF/INFT` rule at line 206.

**maintainer repro — reversal labelled as bounce** · `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98`
The offsetting-credit rule compared the description against `shift(periods=2)` (two rows back) instead of the matching debit one row back, so it never matched and the next rule stamped `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`. Fixed to `shift(periods=1)`, identical to the same rule in ICICI/Saraswat.

## Verification
No tests exist in the repo, so I ran a synthetic-row harness (`/tmp/opencode/verify_enrichment.py`) directly against both bank scripts: 17 checks covering the five complaint shapes plus regression rows (ordinary UPI/IMPS parties, `BIL/ONL` payees, 5-field `INF/INFT`, non-keyword debit/credit pairs that must stay bounces, non-zero-padded 16-digit refs that must stay transfers).

- **After fix:** all 17 pass.
- **Before fix** (via `git stash`): exactly the 7 checks corresponding to the complaints fail — reproducing each post verbatim (numeric ref lifted into the name, empty/wrong counterparty, bounce instead of reversal) — while every "already correct" row is byte-identical before and after.
